data.description:

data.title: S&P cuts Poland's local-currency rating, revises outlook to 'negative' on rising debt
data.description:
Credit ratings agency S&P Global lowered Poland's long- and short-term local currency sovereign credit ratings to "A-/A-2" from "A/A-1", citing elevated budgetary deficits and rising government debt that could constrain policy flexibility in the face of future shocks.

S&P also revised the country's outlook to "negative" from "stable".

The move comes as concerns over Poland's public finances intensify, with the finance ministry forecasting in September that general government debt will rise to 69.3% of gross domestic product in 2027 from 67.6% in 2026 and reach 76.6% by 2030, while debt-servicing costs could approach 3% of GDP by the end of the decade.

S&P warned that Poland's rising debt burden could eventually force the government into sharp fiscal consolidation by 2029 and 2030, as the country approaches its constitutional debt limits.

Despite these concerns, S&P said Poland's recent resilience to external pressures reflects its diversified economy, flexible labor and product markets, educated workforce, and access to ample nondebt-creating external funding.

S&P's action comes less than two months after peer Moody's downgraded Poland's sovereign rating, citing deteriorating fiscal strength as large budget deficits and higher borrowing costs drove a surge in government debt ahead of next year's parliamentary election.

S&P also maintained Poland's long- and short-term foreign currency sovereign ratings at "A-/A-2".

data.title: KARNALYTE RESOURCES INC. ANNOUNCES 2026 THIRD QUARTER RESULTS AND CORPORATE HIGHLIGHTS
data.description:
/NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION TO U.S. NEWS WIRE SERVICES OR DISSEMINATION IN THE UNITED STATES./

SASKATOON, SK, Nov. 6, 2026 /CNW/ -- Karnalyte Resources Inc. ("Karnalyte" or the "Company") () today announced its financial results and corporate highlights for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Q3 2026 HIGHLIGHTS

During the quarter, Karnalyte continued to advance initiatives supporting the development of its Wynyard Potash Project (the "Wynyard Project" or the "Project"), with a focus on development planning, infrastructure requirements, strategic partnerships and financing activities.

Karnalyte continued to evaluate its development strategy for the Wynyard Project, including alternative development approaches and opportunities to optimize project scope, capital requirements and execution strategies. These efforts are intended to support a practical and financially sustainable approach to advancing the Project toward development.

"We continue to focus on advancing the Wynyard Project through a disciplined approach to development planning, strategic engagement and financing," said Danielle Favreau, Chief Executive Officer of Karnalyte Resources Inc. "Our engagement with GSFC and government stakeholders during the quarter provided valuable opportunities to discuss the Project's development requirements and strengthen important relationships. As we move forward, our priorities remain focused on optimizing the development strategy, addressing near-term financing requirements and establishing a viable path toward the next phase of the Project."

During the quarter, Karnalyte welcomed senior representatives of Gujarat State Fertilizers and Chemicals Limited ("GSFC"), the Company's strategic partner and significant shareholder, to Saskatchewan.

The visit included a tour of the Wynyard Project site and meetings with local and provincial government officials, as well as representatives of provincial utility providers. Discussions focused on the Project's development plans, infrastructure requirements and potential economic benefits.

These engagements provided an opportunity to strengthen relationships with key stakeholders and reinforce the importance of continued collaboration in supporting the future development of the Wynyard Project.

The Company continued to advance its rail infrastructure study during the quarter, including the evaluation of potential rail access routes and associated infrastructure requirements.

The study is intended to inform future development planning and support the integration of transportation infrastructure into the Project's overall execution strategy.

Karnalyte continued to pursue financing initiatives to address its near-term working capital requirements and support the longer-term development of the Wynyard Project.

During the quarter, the Company engaged in discussions regarding potential short-term debt financing to support its working capital requirements and provide additional financial flexibility as it advances project development planning and financing initiatives.

In parallel, Karnalyte continued to explore strategic financing opportunities and potential funding structures to support the next stages of engineering and development activities.

The Company remains focused on establishing a comprehensive financing strategy that considers the Project's capital requirements, development sequencing and potential participation by strategic and financial partners.

ASSET SALES

Subsequent to the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Karnalyte completed the sale of a parcel of farmland in the Wynyard area for net proceeds of $504,000.

This transaction follows the sale of three parcels of farmland completed during the second quarter of 2026, which generated aggregate net proceeds of approximately $1.6 million.

The land dispositions form part of the Company's ongoing efforts to optimize its asset portfolio, support working capital requirements and align its land holdings with the future development needs of the Wynyard Project.

Karnalyte continues to evaluate additional land dispositions in accordance with the updated exemption order received from the Saskatchewan Farm Land Security Board on March 24, 2026, while taking into consideration the land access requirements necessary for future Project development.

OUTLOOK FOR 2026

For the remainder of 2026, Karnalyte intends to maintain its focus on advancing the Wynyard Project through disciplined development planning, technical evaluation, stakeholder engagement and financing initiatives.

The Company's principal priorities include:

  • Continuing to refine the Project's development strategy, including opportunities to optimize project scope, capital requirements and development sequencing;
  • Advancing technical and infrastructure studies, including rail access planning and associated infrastructure requirements;
  • Evaluating opportunities to advance the development of magnesium products associated with the Wynyard deposit;
  • Pursuing strategic partnerships, financing arrangements and other business development opportunities to support future engineering and project development activities; and
  • Maintaining disciplined management of working capital, corporate expenditures and capital allocation.

Karnalyte remains committed to advancing the Wynyard Project in a responsible and financially disciplined manner. The Company believes that continued optimization of its development strategy, engagement with strategic partners and stakeholders, and progress toward securing financing will be important to positioning the Project for future development and creating long-term shareholder value.

2026 THIRD QUARTER RESULTS

At September 30, 2026, the Company had cash of $0.3 million and positive working capital of $0.8 million. The Company has no debt. Karnalyte's Third Quarter 2026 Financial Statements and Managements' Discussion and Analysis are available at www.sedarplus.com and on Karnalyte's website at www.karnalyte.com.

ABOUT KARNALYTE RESOURCES INC.

Karnalyte Resources Inc. is a development stage potash company. Karnalyte owns the Wynyard Project, with planned Phase 1 production of 675,000 t/a of high grade granular potash, and two subsequent phases of 750,000 t/a each, taking total production up to 2.175 million t/a. All environmental permits remain valid, preliminary detailed engineering is complete, and the existing Offtake Agreement with GSFC remains in effect. Karnalyte is also considering opportunities relating to secondary magnesium compounds. Further development is dependent on the continued strength of potash prices and obtaining financing.

ABOUT GUJARAT STATE FERTILIZERS & CHEMICALS LIMITED

GSFC is a leading Indian Fortune 500 chemicals and fertilizer company that has been in business for more than 60 years. GSFC currently operates one ammonia plant that was commissioned in the year 2000, and two urea plants that were established in 1969, at its fertilizer production complex in Vadodara, Gujarat State, India. GSFC is the Company's strategic partner and single largest shareholder.

data.title: Constellation Software Reports Higher 3Q Profit Boosted by Acquisitions
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Constellation Software reported higher profit and growing revenue in the third quarter, boosted by contributions from acquired businesses.

The company, whose business model involves acquiring smaller software firms, on Friday logged a profit of $212 million, or $10.01 a share. That compares with a profit of $210 million, or $9.89 a share, a year earlier. Analysts polled by FactSet were expecting earnings of $15.17 a share.

Revenue grew 19% to $3.51 billion. Analysts were expecting $3.50 billion. The growth was driven largely by acquisitions, with organic revenue growing 2% during the quarter, Constellation said.

Maintenance and other recurring revenue, which makes up most of the company's topline, rose to $2.72 billion from $2.21 billion a year prior. Professional services revenue rose to $569 million from $538 million, and hardware and other revenue rose to $131 million from $89 million.

Licensing revenue declined to $97 million from $107 million.

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com
